newsitem.title: UK: UK 1996 government deficit 4.4 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: UK 1996 government deficit 4.4 pct of GDP.

text.p: Britain's general government financial deficit was 4.4 percent of GDP in 1996, the Office for National Statistics said on Thursday.
This compares with a ratio of 5.6 percent in 1995 and 6.8 percent in 1994.
General government gross debt in 1996 was 54.8 percent of GDP, the ONS said, up from 54.2 in 1995 and 50.5 in 1994.

The government debt estimates are made under the terms of the Maastricht Treaty which set a reference value for countries wishing to sign up for a European single currency of a budget deficit below or moving towards three percent of GDP.
The Treaty also set a reference level for overall government debt of 60 percent of GDP.
For consistency with other European Union nations, the figures are reported on a calendar year basis although Britain's public finances are planned on a financial year.
The figures on deficit and debt are reported twice a year to Eurostat, in February and August. Thursday's figures will make up the August report.
